title: Six years with his own band; teaming with Joe Williams
summary: Jimmy Forrest stayed throughout; when Joe Williams left Basie, Basie and Willard Alexander paired him with Edison for a successful double bill.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: -- get to? Oh, we were finishing off the group, when you had Jimmy Forrest,
Oh, yeah, Jimmy Forrest. Then he stayed with me the whole time I had a band.
And how long was that?
Oh, I had a band for about six years.
Wow. Were you --
From '57 -- well, then, you know, when Joe Williams left Basie, Will Alexander was handling me and Basie put the both of us together, Joe Williams.
Oh, Basie did that.

Yeah, Basie did that, because he was managing Joe Williams at the time, see? And naturally, I played the same -- the mainstream music that Basie did. So they figured it would be a good marriage there, you know? Joe Williams and myself, you know.
Yeah, it was.
So he put us together and it was successful. But I think I should have continued on as a soloist, you know.
(Recording interruption.)
When the two of you get together like that -- do you mean Joe was getting almost too much of the
attention then?
Not really. We were both -- we both had out time to play. Like he would do a half hour and I would do a half hour, something like that.
Well, would you play first?
I would play first.
Then he comes out.
Then he would come out. And I would introduce him, you know. And it was a good show. It was something that should have stayed together, what everybody says.
Yeah.
